cds.text: Understand that complex sentences have one independent clause and at least one dependent clause, joined by subordinating conjunctions to show time and cause
Understand that a complex sentence has a main clause and at least one dependent clause, and how writers use this for effect
Understand how embedded clauses expand complex sentences to elaborate, extend and explain ideas
Investigate how quoted (direct) and reported (indirect) speech are used
Understand how noun groups can be expanded to give fuller descriptions of a person, place, thing or idea
Understand how ideas can be expanded and sharpened through verb choice, elaborated tenses and adverb groups
Understand how adverb groups and prepositional phrases give circumstantial details about an activity
Understand past, present and future tenses and their impact on meaning in a sentence
Understand quotation marks signal dialogue, dialogue capitalisation conventions, and commas and boundary punctuation
Use commas to set off prepositional phrases, and apostrophes for multiple possession
Use commas for lists, to separate a dependent clause from an independent clause, and in dialogue
Read and write words with more complex letter combinations, including a variety of vowel sounds and known prefixes and suffixes
Use phoneme-grapheme matches, syllables and common letter patterns that have different pronunciations to read and write words
Apply phonological and morphological knowledge to read and write increasingly complex words
Use letter patterns (including double letters), spelling generalisations, word families, prefixes, suffixes and word origins to spell more complex words
Build and spell new words from known words, base words, prefixes, suffixes, word origins, letter patterns and spelling generalisations
Spell new words, including technical words, using word origins (including Latin and Greek roots), base words, affixes, letter patterns and generalisations
Read and write high-frequency words, including homophones, and use context to identify correct spelling
Explore less common plurals, and understand how a suffix changes a word's meaning or grammatical form

sentences.text: {{S}} automatically uses strategies in a range of contexts to spell unfamiliar words.
{{S}} identifies complex letter patterns and sounds when spelling and applies this knowledge to improve spelling accuracy.
{{S}} applies spelling generalisations to spell most familiar and less common words correctly.
{{S}} selects appropriate tenses to suit different writing tasks.
{{S}} applies familiar spelling patterns and is working towards greater accuracy when spelling less common words.
{{S}} spells familiar words by using common letter patterns and recognising the sounds in words.
{{S}} checks {{pos}} work for spelling mistakes and uses dictionaries to correct them.
{{S}} uses commas to separate parts of a sentence and apostrophes for contractions.
{{S}} varies sentence length to improve {{pos}} writing.

rows.newText: {{S}} writes complex sentences with a main clause and one or more dependent clauses.
{{S}} varies sentence structure by joining main and dependent clauses in different orders.
{{S}} uses embedded clauses to elaborate, extend and explain ideas in complex sentences.
{{S}} adds detail to a sentence by embedding a clause within it.
{{S}} expands noun groups to give fuller descriptions of people, places and things.
{{S}} writes noun groups that include adjectives and phrases to describe in detail.
{{S}} sharpens ideas through precise verb choices and elaborated tenses.
{{S}} selects verbs and tenses that add precision and meaning to a sentence.
{{S}} uses commas to set off prepositional phrases and apostrophes for multiple possessors.
{{S}} uses apostrophes correctly when more than one owner is involved.
{{S}} uses commas in lists and to separate a dependent clause from a main clause.
{{S}} checks punctuation to make sure that clauses are separated clearly.
{{S}} uses sounds, syllables and common letter patterns to read and spell words with different pronunciations.
{{S}} applies phonological and morphological knowledge to spell increasingly complex words.
{{S}} breaks complex words into syllables and meaningful parts to spell them.
{{S}} builds and spells new words from known words, base words, prefixes and suffixes.
{{S}} uses word origins and letter patterns to spell new and technical words.
{{S}} spells technical words using what {{s}} knows about Latin and Greek roots.
{{S}} explores less common plurals and explains how a suffix changes a word.
{{S}} spells less common plurals correctly and understands how suffixes change meaning.
